title: NIST AI TEVV Program — Phase 65 NIST ARIA assurance adoption review
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the NIST ARIA assurance adoption reporting pack. NIST identifies test, evaluation, validation, and verification as a measurement-science program for trustworthy AI.
key_findings: The program connects measurement science to AI risk management.
It exposes tools, evaluations, and standards work.
It does not certify named deployments.
why_it_matters: Which records connect evaluation design and authorization to monitoring, incidents, correction, independent review, institutional use, and outcomes? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It clarifies the institutional home for turning assurance principles into repeatable methods.
ftfn_relevance: Advances one named Phase 55Y reader journey.
Separates the current evidence stage from downstream operation or outcome claims.
Creates a specific next-record watch point.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
Program activity is upstream of system authorization and operating evidence.
No universal TEVV method is established.
